chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Storefront advertising bands on the corner
summary: Shops hired local bands, such as the Superior Band, Buddy Petit or Chris Kelly, to draw crowds.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: It went on and on. Some sounds. It's not like you're in some little country town. Because this was a business city. And there was commerce and things going on, and you observed it. And then they would advertise... There was a plentiful supply of musicians, so if you would open up a little store, you would get a little local band, whether it was a Spasm band or a Jazz band or whatever you... And there was a band out there playing. When the people heard that bass drum beating that bass line, they'd run outside, left their food burning on the table, just run out there to

see what the hell is happening. And there on the corner would be maybe the Superior Band, or Buddy Petit's band, or Chris Kelly's band playing out there. And you'd go out there to look at the music. Because there was music. Everything was music.
